podcast.body: This album, released in 1965, was a collection of orchestral covers of Rolling Stones songs, including an interpretation of "The Last Time." These arrangements were often "watered down" versions, designed for easy listening fans who might be offended by rock and roll music. A five-note progression from their version of "The Last Time" later became the basis for The Verve's "Bittersweet Symphony." "The Rolling Stones songbook, a collection of covers by the Andrew Luege Oldham Orchestra, released in 1965."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released by Andrew Loog Oldham, then manager of The Rolling Stones, this album featured orchestral instrumental arrangements of Stones songs for the easy-listening crowd. It contained a version of "The Last Time" with a six-second string figure arranged by David Whitaker that was central to The Verve's "Bittersweet Symphony" lawsuit. "In 1966, he released the Rolling Stones songbook under the name The Andrew Lou Geoldem Orchestra, and it featured this version of the 1965 Stone Song The Last Time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
